transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been getting out of breath going up the stairs. It's been bothering me more lately.
Can you tell me when you first noticed this, whether it came on suddenly or gradually, what you were doing when it started, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It came on gradually, I think — a while back now. And no, I've never had any trouble with medicines as far as I know.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means it doesn't bother you at all and 10 means it's the worst it could be, how much does getting out of breath on the stairs affect you day to day?
Oh, I couldn't put a number on it. It's not too bad, but I do have to stop and catch my breath.
Could you tell me about any medicines you're taking—regular or new ones—and any past health problems, operations, or hospital stays you've had?

I take a few tablets — one in the morning and some with my evening meal — my wife keeps track of them better than I do. As for my health, I had a heart attack some years back, and I've got an irregular heartbeat.
When you get out of breath on the stairs, is there anything else you notice happening at the same time?
Well, I've noticed my ankles get a bit puffy by the evening, and I've started using two pillows at night instead of one. No chest pain or anything like that, though.
When you get out of breath going up the stairs, where in your body do you feel it, and does it move anywhere or stay in one place?
I just feel it in my chest really, like I can't get enough air in. It doesn't move anywhere, it's just there until I rest.
What worries you most about this, and what are you hoping we can do for you today?
I'm worried about managing the stairs to get up to bed, and I'd like to know whether my heart is getting worse.
Besides the heart attack and irregular heartbeat you mentioned, is there anything else about your past health, operations, or hospital stays you’d like to add?
I did have a scan of my heart at the hospital last year, but I can't remember what they said about it. Nothing else I can think of, no operations.
Are there any other things you've noticed along with the breathlessness, or anything else you'd like to add?
I don't think so. Just the puffiness in the ankles and needing the extra pillow. No cough or fever or anything.
When did you first notice getting out of breath on the stairs — did it come on suddenly or build up gradually, and was anything going on at the time?
It built up gradually, over about three months now that I think about it. Nothing special was going on — it just got worse little by little.
Can you tell me what medicines you take regularly, and if any have been started or changed recently, including the dose if you know it?

I take a blood thinner — rivaroxaban, I think it's called — with my evening meal. And bisoprolol in the morning, plus atorvastatin at night and ramipril. I'm not sure of the doses, my wife would know better.
Is there anything else about your medicines you'd like to add — anything you take that we haven't talked about yet?
No, that's the lot — four tablets as far as I know.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
